mem.10:
27 March 2023: Audrey and Andrew caught up. Andrew had started a Financial Analyst job the previous week. Audrey had three dogs—Pepper, Precious and Panda—whom she’d had for three years and adored. They explored parks and trails; she shared a photo of two in new collars. Andrew had no pets, loved animals and was fascinated by eagles. He shared a photo of birds flying against the sun; he spotted birds while hiking but hadn’t bird-watched. He recommended Fox Hollow for a weekend hike; Audrey planned to try it.

2 April 2023: Audrey’s household had adopted Pixie, a small white puppy, making four dogs. Caring for Pixie had kept Audrey busy, so she hadn’t visited the previously discussed hiking spot. Pixie needed a few days to adjust; Pepper had also taken time but was now always with her. Audrey shared photos of the dogs playing and relaxing, including one dog lying on a couch with a pillow; she called them good cuddle companions. Her nearby park was great for walking her pup. Andrew shared a photo of his family dog sitting on a living-room couch. He was considering adopting but struggled to find dog-friendly city housing. Audrey said websites with pet filters had helped her household find a suitable place; Andrew planned to try them. He missed hiking with his family’s dog and said dog hikes build bonds and memories. Audrey hoped to hike with her dogs; Andrew promised updates.

16 April 2023: Andrew and his girlfriend had tried a city cafe. He enjoyed it but missed nature’s peace and sense of connection; it helped him reset when life was chaotic. Audrey said dog walks helped her recharge. Andrew shared a bakery photo (croissants, muffins, tarts, coffee). Audrey had baked blueberry muffins and proposed a pastry party; Andrew enthusiastically agreed. Audrey said her dogs would come. She shared a dog-and-sunflowers tattoo on her arm, explaining it represented her love of her dogs and nature and let her see their faces when they weren’t there; also shared a woman walking dogs in woods.

3 May 2023: Audrey had hiked the previous week and saw a hummingbird (shared photo, wings spread on a branch). Andrew found nearby open space and tried to get out of the city weekly; shared sunset lake and mountain photos. They found nature therapeutic and agreed small positive gestures bring joy. Audrey’s energetic dogs loved hikes, new scents, fetch with ball/frisbee, and dog-park playdates; she enjoyed chatting with owners. She shared photos of dogs in a field, playing, one catching a frisbee, and one wearing a party hat on a couch. Dogs tolerate party hats, which Audrey puts on them for fun and treats. She stressed safety (one wore shoes and leash), and recommended a nearby dog park with trees/benches; Andrew would check it out.

6 May 2023: Andrew was still searching for a dog to adopt, browsing websites, visiting shelters and asking friends. He found the process fun but frustrating; shared a dog looking through a cage. Audrey shared dogs running in a field, one carrying a ball. Andrew suggested matching dog size/breed and exercise needs to living space and lifestyle. Pet-friendly housing remained difficult; he contacted landlords and sought a place near parks or woods. On 5 May Audrey and her dogs took a road trip to a national park; shared three dogs running in grass. They took road trips every couple of months. Andrew added a dog road trip to his bucket list and planned to visit another shelter soon and update Audrey.

11 May 2023: Andrew hiked with friends and girlfriend at a nearby spot; shared a dirt path to a grassy hill. Audrey had signed up for a positive-reinforcement pet-bonding workshop in June and shared a flyer/photo of dogs, one circled yellow. She found the flyer at a local pet store and met a friendly, playful dog there. She expected her quick-learning, reward-loving dogs to do well and opposed punishment; even thinking of hurting a dog pained her. Andrew agreed and said he’d look into positive-reinforcement classes. Audrey would report back and offer tips for his future dog.

2 June 2023: Audrey’s dogs had played off-leash at a park the previous day. The previous week they reached a beautiful national-park peak at sunset; she described it as paradise and unforgettable, with dogs running and birds chirping. Shared several photos, including two horses in a fenced field. She said nature cheers her up and makes her feel grateful. Andrew was still searching for a dog and dog-friendly housing, discouraged but determined; Audrey offered help if he emailed his criteria.

13 June 2023: Andrew and friends took a rock-climbing class the previous Sunday. He reached the top, found it challenging but satisfying, and felt proud; shared a summit view and a man climbing. He hoped to try outdoor activities weekly, including kayaking and perhaps bungee jumping. Audrey congratulated him and said nature reminds us how tiny we are. She found a small wooded park trail and invited him; he accepted. Her dogs usually walked about an hour, exploring at their own pace; walks were their favorite part of the day. They loved meeting dogs and got excited when she brought out a ball or frisbee. Audrey called dogs and nature her happy place; Andrew said nature calmed and refreshed him.

26 June 2023: Audrey had moved to a place with a bigger backyard and set up dog agility equipment and toys; shared two dogs on the lawn. Andrew shared a nearby doggy daycare photo; Audrey wanted to visit and he offered to find more dog-friendly places. They agreed pets are family and bring joy. Audrey was still unpacking. Andrew shared a flower bed and described a hike the previous Friday, enjoying birdsong and the smell of trees. Audrey shared photos of feet resting on a rock above a lake and someone sitting above a mountain lake; recalled a peaceful lake hike with friends years earlier. They agreed nature soothes, recharges, and small things shouldn’t be taken for granted.

3 July 2023: Audrey was taking a challenging but rewarding dog-training course; dogs were improving, though it took much of her time and limited new trail trips. Andrew still couldn’t find dog-friendly housing and had life “curveballs”; he’d switched to urban adventures. Audrey shared two dogs running in a field with a ball. Her four dogs were all 3 years old: two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes, all mutts. They loved running and fetch, were a great pack, and had a somewhat crazy but fun doggy playdate the previous Friday. She shared photos of two curled in a dog bed and two on a couch under a blanket, and called them her universe.

Andrew had recently taken up cooking and experimenting with recipes to relax and be creative; he was a rookie. Audrey loved cooking as an escape and creative outlet. Her favorite recipe was family chicken pot pie, a cozy dish that reminded her of her grandmother’s kitchen and conversations at the table; she shared pie photos and offered to send the recipe. Audrey enjoyed music, wine and going with the flow while cooking, calling it therapeutic self-care. Garlic was her go-to ingredient. She offered Andrew her roasted-chicken recipe, shared a photo of chicken and potatoes, and said it was inspired by Mediterranean flavors: chicken, garlic, lemon and herbs; an easy, healthy comfort meal. Andrew looked forward to trying both recipes and promised to report back.
mem.19:
27 Mar 2023: Audrey and Andrew caught up. Andrew had started a Financial Analyst job the previous week; he had no pets, loved animals (especially eagles), shared a bird-silhouette photo and recommended Fox Hollow for hiking. Audrey had Pepper, Precious and Panda, loved parks/trails, and shared dog photos.

2 Apr: Audrey’s household adopted Pixie, a small white puppy, bringing them to four dogs. Caring for Pixie kept Audrey from visiting a previously discussed hiking spot. Andrew missed hiking nature trails with his family dog (shared photos of a man walking a dog on a trail and sitting on a rock with a dog); he said dog hikes build bonds and memories. Audrey’s dogs were good cuddle companions (shared couch-and-pillow photo). Andrew wanted a dog but city housing was difficult; Audrey suggested pet-friendly housing sites.

8–9 Apr: Andrew and girlfriend liked exploring city cafés and trying new things.

16 Apr: Andrew shared a café photo of coffee and pastries; he and girlfriend had croissants, muffins and tarts at a place with irresistible-smelling pastries. Audrey missed nature, walked dogs to recharge, baked blueberry muffins and suggested a pastry party. She shared her dog-and-sunflower arm tattoo and walking photos.

3 May: Audrey shared hummingbird photo; Andrew shared sunset lake/mountain photos and said local hikes refreshed him. He aimed to get outside weekly and spot birds. Both found nature therapeutic. Audrey’s city dogs loved hikes, new scents, parks, fetch, frisbees and dog-park playdates; their faces brightened when she prepared walks, their favorite part of the day. She recommended a shady dog park with benches. Andrew shared a dirt path to a grassy hill.

5–6 May: Audrey and dogs road-tripped to a national park every couple months. Andrew searched for a dog via websites, friends and shelters, considering size, breed, exercise needs, housing rules and outdoor access. Audrey’s dogs enjoyed exploring nature; wagging tails showed their excitement.

11 May: Andrew hiked with friends and girlfriend. Audrey enrolled in a June positive-reinforcement pet-bonding workshop; opposed punishment. Her dogs learned quickly and loved treats; Andrew considered classes.

26 May–1 Jun: Audrey hiked with dogs to a national-park peak; sunset, breeze and birdsong felt like a slice of paradise and lifted her mood. 1 Jun: dogs played off-leash at a park. By 2 Jun, Andrew had checked pet-friendly city housing without success, felt discouraged but remained determined to find the right home and dog.

11 Jun: Andrew, a beginner, took a rock-climbing class with friends, reached the top, and found it challenging, satisfying and fantastic; friends’ encouragement helped. He hoped for weekly outdoor activities, kayaking and perhaps bungee jumping. Audrey invited him to a wooded park trail; he accepted. Her dogs walked about an hour, met dogs and fetched. Both called nature/dogs their happy place.

23 Jun: Andrew hiked with friends in good weather, took photos but had not reviewed them by 26 Jun. Audrey had a nearby park for walking her pup. Years earlier she and friends had sat by a peaceful mountain lake, talking and admiring nature; she found it calming. Audrey shared dogs on a rock by a lake and said they enjoyed mountain life.

26 Jun: Audrey moved to a house with a bigger backyard, agility equipment and toys. Andrew offered to find dog-friendly places. Audrey had taken a dog-grooming course.

30 Jun: Audrey’s doggy playdate was a bit crazy but lots of fun.

3 Jul: Audrey’s challenging training course improved behavior but left little time for trails. Four 3-year-old mutts: two Jack Russell mixes, two Chihuahua mixes. Personalities: oldest relaxed “wise sage,” second playful, third naughty/cuddly, youngest lively/adventurous. Dogs were her universe; caring for them fulfilled her. They tolerate party hats, which she uses for fun and treats. Andrew began cooking to relax. Audrey’s favorite chicken pot pie was her grandmother’s recipe; she offered it. She liked cooking with music, wine and improvisation; go-to ingredient garlic. Favorite comfort food: Mediterranean roasted chicken with garlic, lemon and herbs; offered recipe.

7–8 Jul: Andrew picnicked with girlfriend on 7 Jul, enjoying snacks and drinks. Still seeking dog-friendly housing; Audrey found a nearby breeder. Andrew wanted open space for a dog and planned an August hike, checking trail safety. Audrey shared steep coastal-trail map/photos and a mountain/lake sunset from a hike three hours away.

11 Jul: Andrew adopted German Shepherd puppy Toby despite city living. Work overload made him miss hiking. Audrey invited him to hike together with pups in August; he accepted. She shared engraved wooden dog tags/keychains personalized to each dog’s personality.

27 Jul: Andrew and girlfriend volunteered at a shelter Monday; rewarding. Audrey might volunteer someday but prioritizes her four dogs. Andrew shared tennis-ball dog photo; Audrey identified childhood dog Max, energetic and fond of fetch, and recalled telling him worries and hopes on walks.

4 Aug: Andrew planned weekend camping with girlfriend and Toby. Audrey started agility classes twice weekly; dogs liked challenges and socializing. She shared agility and two-hour hike photos. Andrew found fresh air, trees and summits calming. Audrey said pets supported her through tough times and bring joy and companionship. She advised time, attention and walks for high-energy Toby; Andrew planned a small local hike.

16 Aug: Audrey got tattoo of all four dogs; four were enough to give them attention. Vet visits with all four were chaotic, so next time one at a time. Resting spots: Pepper couch, Pixie bed, Precious chair, Panda rug. Both shared pet-snuggling photos and saw pets as family.

19–20 Aug: Andrew visited a new café during a work break on 19 Aug. Audrey planned a park stroll with dogs for the weekend; good exercise for them.

24 Aug: Andrew and girlfriend fished at a nearby lake the previous weekend and caught a few fish. Audrey had never fished; recalled peaceful mountain-lake outing with friends and shared dogs by a lake. She described dog care (brushing, baths, nail trims, affection) as serious but rewarding. Andrew wanted a strong bond with Toby, shared photos including Toby asleep in a bed and a small dog with leash; Audrey said allow time, don’t rush. Andrew wanted to work it out himself first; they anticipated outdoor adventures.

2–3 Sep: Andrew hiked to escape the city and saw a beautiful sunset; shared photo of a person on a mountain with city view. Toby was still too young to hike. Andrew still struggled to find dog-friendly housing; Audrey urged persistence.

6 Sep: Andrew said stressful work disrupted outdoor time; he recharged with morning coffee and lunchtime walks. Audrey encouraged self-care and did at least one daily activity for herself. She organized neighborhood dog playdate (photo of two dogs in fenced area); their joy made her happy. The prior week she bought beds for cooler weather (photo of dog on living-room bed); dogs liked curling up.

24 Sep: Audrey said a dog (Andrew guessed Precious) pulled so hard at the park the previous Friday that the leash broke; she chased and caught her before harm. Shared red retractable leash photo. She soothed the dog with petting, hugs, calm speech and a slow walk. Andrew wanted a bond like hers with Toby. Audrey advised patience, regular training, love and praise. She trains obedience and tricks (sit, stay, shake, roll over); walks dogs multiple times daily for exercise/bonding. All four are mutts: two Jack Russell mixes, two Chihuahua mixes. Dogs play in her garden and with each other; just her own “fur babies.” Andrew shared balcony flowers; Audrey has a small garden, flower beds and veggie patch. Her Peruvian Lilies are easy-care, needing water and sun. Dogs mean everything to her. Various photos were shared: dogs in party hats, on beds/couches, at beach, running in fields, and cuddling.
mem.28:
27 Mar 2023: Audrey and Andrew reconnected. Andrew had just become a Financial Analyst, lived in the city, missed nature and wanted a dog but faced housing constraints. He loves animals, especially eagles, shared a bird-silhouette photo, and recommended Fox Hollow hiking trail. Audrey has dogs and loves parks, trails and sharing their photos.

2 Apr: Audrey’s household adopted white puppy Pixie, who bonded with Pepper. Audrey suggested pet-friendly housing sites and considering a dog’s space/exercise needs; Andrew hoped to find a dog-friendly place and explore trails with a dog. They shared couch-dog photos. Andrew and his girlfriend like discovering cafés and unwinding after busy weeks; on the weekend of 8–9 Apr they tried a new city café.

Audrey cooks creatively with music and wine (blueberry muffins, grandmother’s chicken pot pie, garlic-heavy Mediterranean roasted chicken). Her dog-and-sunflower tattoo reflects her love of dogs and nature. Andrew enjoys cooking but is a beginner. Audrey’s four mixed-breed dogs are family and bring her joy, love and happiness. Breed descriptions vary: she described Pepper and Panda as Lab mixes and Precious and Pixie as Chihuahua mixes; another account says two Jack Russell mixes and two Chihuahua mixes. She says she has four dogs (11 May) and spends much of her free time caring for them. Their personalities: oldest a relaxed “wise sage,” second playful, third naughty/cuddly, youngest lively/adventurous. They enjoy hiking, scents, nature, parks, fetch/frisbees, playdates and shade; their wagging tails show how much they enjoy hikes. Audrey walks them several times daily, usually about an hour, and road-trips with them to national parks every few months. She moved to a house with a bigger yard in June and has agility gear, toys and nearby indoor daycare. She took a grooming course; handles ears/paws gently, uses party hats/treats, and has tattooed all four dogs. Vet visits are chaotic: after taking them all on 16 Aug, she planned one at a time. Favorite resting spots: Pepper couch, Pixie bed, Precious chair, Panda rug. Childhood dog Max loved fetch and was her walking confidant. Audrey hopes her dogs recover fully and can hike again.

Apr–Jun: Audrey finds outdoor time with dogs peaceful and inspiring—her happy place. She recalled a calming mountain-lake hike with friends years earlier and an amazing sunset at a scenic place three hours away. She photographed a hummingbird (2 Jun), loves birds’ freedom, and planned to learn local birds before birdwatching with Andrew; he planned binoculars and a bird notebook. Andrew had not gone specifically birdwatching but noticed birds hiking. Audrey offered (2 Jun) to help him find a dog and asked him to email criteria. On 1 Jun she watched dogs run off leash at a park; 5 May she road-tripped with them to a national park. She had a doggy playdate 30 Jun, “crazy but lots of fun.” Her recommended dog park, near where she walks, has trees and benches; it’s good for playdates. She shared a favorite hiking photo of two horses in a field. Andrew shared sunset lake/mountain photos, including a mountain church, and hiked with friends 23 Jun. Audrey hiked with her dogs to a national-park peak; sunset, breeze and birdsong restored her. Andrew likes hiking/kayaking, considered bungee jumping, and completed a beginner climbing class, reaching the top.

26 Jun: Audrey was unpacking after moving house; yard has dog play area/agility equipment and nearby indoor daycare. Andrew and Audrey agreed to hike with her dogs in August when weather was pleasant. Andrew suggested a trail and shared its map; Audrey planned to look into it. They hoped dogs could run freely but would ensure trail safety. No date/place or confirmed hike recorded.

Jul–Aug: Andrew adopted German Shepherd puppy Toby; he and girlfriend volunteered at a shelter. Audrey advised patience, positive reinforcement, daily exercise/socialization, walks, training, praise and love; she expected her quick-learning dogs to respond to rewards and offered future tips. On 24 Aug she said bonding with Toby takes time and offered advice. Andrew had long wanted to learn grooming but lacked time. On 11 Jul he invited Audrey and dogs hiking with Toby in August; she accepted, unspecified date/location. He shared engraved wooden dog tags/keychains. Audrey does agility twice weekly and might adopt more someday; she might volunteer but prioritizes her dogs. Andrew planned Toby camping and fished with his girlfriend; Audrey had never fished. 4 Aug they discussed nature’s calming effect and German Shepherd activity needs. 16 Aug Andrew and girlfriend got vegetables at a farm; Audrey had an outdoor day with dogs. Andrew planned a nature-reserve visit/photos 19–20 Aug, but on 24 Aug said he’d first learn Toby’s care himself. On 18 Aug Andrew took a work break at a new café. On 19 Aug Audrey shared a groomed dog-on-table photo, describing the dogs as soft/fluffy.

Sep: Andrew’s work stress made outdoor activities difficult; coffee/lunch walks helped, and he tried to get out of the city hiking at least weekly. Audrey said (6 Sep) she did at least one self-care activity daily, such as treating herself. Toby was too young to hike and dog-friendly housing remained difficult. Audrey arranged a neighbor playdate and bought cold-weather beds. A dog (Andrew guessed Precious) broke a leash pulling at a park; Audrey safely caught and soothed her. She teaches sit/stay/shake/roll over. Garden has easy-care Peruvian lilies; Andrew shared balcony flowers. On Sat 30 Sep Audrey took dogs to a nearby dog park with grass and shade; they loved it.

30 Sep–Oct: Audrey took dogs to beach and they swam. Andrew and girlfriend planned a November beach trip with Toby; he shared ocean sunset. Andrew offered river biking routes; Audrey wanted to see them. Audrey recycles, usually takes transit, and makes jewelry from bottle caps, buttons and broken jewelry, sells it and donates some proceeds to an animal shelter; she couldn’t volunteer. Both value ecology. Audrey recalled dogs running in a field while she recovered from a knee injury. Andrew and girlfriend had board-game night (Tuesday before 13 Oct); Audrey baked neighbors treats to thank them for pup-friendly homes. On 4 Oct Audrey offered plant advice. On 13 Oct Andrew recommended a newly opened scenic café, unsure if dogs were allowed; dog park nearby, coffee suggested. Toby is active, likes sweaters, once chased a squirrel around a tree. Audrey’s dogs enjoy sniffing, fetch/frisbee and parks; snow confused them and they prefer sunny grass. Audrey shared dog photos; added a flower to her tattoo, no more planned unless adopting. Andrew shared forest-path photo. Andrew and girlfriend found a café with irresistible pastries; had croissants, muffins and tarts, and he shared pastry/coffee photo.

19 Oct: Audrey bought dogs toys the prior Monday; their excitement reminded her of their joy and love. Andrew adopted shelter pup Buddy, shared couch/food-bowl photo, hoped he and Toby would be friends. Buddy likes walks and trails; Andrew enjoys walking him and exploring new trails with him and others. Andrew shared dirt road, cow and red truck in a field; Audrey offered a remote hike. Audrey looked forward to hiking with Andrew and dogs next month. On 24 Oct she had a park accident and injured/broke an arm; wore a cast, improving, managed dog care one-handed. Andrew tried local sushi; on 24 Oct planned California/salmon rolls with sauces, different sushi and photos for Audrey. The previous weekend he and girlfriend had wine tasting.

28 Oct: Audrey took dogs to an animal behaviorist the previous Wednesday after unusual behavior. Visit was hectic; exam/questions led to suggested routine changes. She uses positive reinforcement; dogs showed progress but issue wasn’t fully resolved. Andrew encouraged her.
